## What is a Roboflow Workflow?

A pretrained model returns raw predictions — bounding boxes, class names, confidence scores. A real application usually needs more: filtering results, counting objects, drawing overlays, or triggering downstream actions.

A **Workflow** is Roboflow's way of wiring those steps together visually. You connect **blocks** (model, filter, visualization, logic) into a pipeline, test it in a debugger, and deploy it through the Inference Server.

Think of it as the **application layer** on top of the model. The lecture slides on [Computer Vision Inference and Deployment](09_roboflow_inference_library.qmd) explain how Workflows fit into the broader Inference ecosystem.

## Your Task

**Goal:** Build and run a simple object-detection Workflow, visualize its output, and understand how you would call it from code.

Follow the official [Hello World tutorial](https://docs.roboflow.com/workflows/tutorials-1/hello-world). It takes about five minutes.

Pick one setup mode:

| Mode | Best for | Requirements |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Cloud connected** | Fastest start | Free [Roboflow account](https://app.roboflow.com/workflows) |
| **Detached** | Local, no account | [Self-hosted Inference Server](https://docs.roboflow.com/deployment/self-hosted/self-hosted) running locally |

::: {.callout-note}
In **Detached** mode, start the server with `inference server start --dev`, then open the Workflow Builder at [localhost:9001/build](http://localhost:9001/build).
:::
